description: P2b (D-135) source table for the 1900 world's money values. Every RUSD value in historical/p2b traces to these rows through scripts/p2b/build-money-calibration.mjs. Status: sourced (read from the cited source), secondary (from a reprint), provisional (no historical counterpart yet; reasoning in note).

sources.title: Consumer Price Index, 1800-
sources.author: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis
sources.notes: Annual averages, 1967 = 100. Pre-1913 values are the Bank's spliced estimates.

sources.title: Annual Report of the Director of the Mint for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 1901: Values of Foreign Coins, January 1, 1901
sources.author: U.S. Treasury, Bureau of the Mint
sources.notes: Values of monetary units in U.S. gold dollars proclaimed under section 25 of the act of August 28, 1894 (pp. 56-57 of the report). Silver-standard units are valued at the silver price of the preceding quarter.

sources.title: Economic Developments and Monetary Policy Responses in Interwar Japan: Evaluation Based on the Taylor Rule, Table 1
sources.author: Masato Shizume, Bank of Japan IMES, Monetary and Economic Studies 20(3), October 2002
sources.notes: Nominal GNP in millions of yen from Ohkawa, Takamatsu and Yamamoto (1974), LTES vol. 1. The table row is labelled 1896-1900; the level is read as the 1900 value (conflict note in the plan).

sources.title: NBER Macrohistory Database, Chapter IV: Prices
sources.author: National Bureau of Economic Research
sources.notes: Monthly wholesale prices; the 1900 value is the mean of the twelve monthly observations listed in each row.

sources.title: 100 Years of U.S. Consumer Spending: Data for the Nation, New York City, and Boston (Report 991), Tables 1, 2 and 5
sources.author: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, May 2006
sources.notes: 1901 Consumer Expenditure Survey of wage-earner families: average family income $750, expenditure $769, of which food $327 and apparel $108; the families had nearly five people.

sources.author: Albert A. Hopkins and A. Russell Bond (eds.)
sources.notes: Secondary reprint of the 1900 census: gainful occupations by group, and the summary of manufactures. To be verified against the Census volumes.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.note: Definition of the pound (equal to the 1900 US pound to six figures).

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.note: US standard bushel weight for wheat.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.note: US standard barrel of flour.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: yards per pound of 28-inch 64x64 print cloth
rows.note: Trade designation of standard Fall River print cloth ('7-yard goods'); provisional until a sourced weight is found.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.note: LABOR_STANDARD_HOURS_PER_WEEK in the constants module.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.note: Full-year employment; the hourly series has no unemployment adjustment.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: farm labour income relative to the production-worker wage
rows.note: USDA Bulletin 94 Table 12 has the 1899 farm wage rates but its scanned text could not be read reliably; 0.5 is provisional pending that table.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: capitalist reference wage relative to salaried officials and clerks
rows.note: No 1900 building employs capitalists; the reference wage only prices construction labour.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: labour share of farm value added
rows.note: Owner-operated farms: the rest of value added is the owner's return to land and capital, paid out as profit to the owning household.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: labour share of manufacturing value added
rows.note: Census 1900 manufactures (reprint): wages about $2.32 bn and salaries about $0.40 bn over products $13.06 bn less materials $7.36 bn and miscellaneous expenses $1.03 bn.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: construction cost of one level, in years of its wage bill at reference wages
rows.note: Order of magnitude of 1900 capital per worker relative to annual pay; no sourced capital stock per building type yet.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: annual upkeep as a share of construction cost
rows.note: Provisional depreciation of structures and equipment.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: days of wages, inputs and upkeep held as operating cash
rows.note: CONSTRUCTION_WORKING_CAPITAL_DAYS in the constants module.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: days of producers' input demand held as opening stock
rows.note: Producers buy inputs only from the opening stock, households can buy the day's output (M3d Pass B), so a market opens with one day of its input demand (D-136); replaces the M11 authored stock lots.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: months of household income held as cash
rows.note: No cross-country 1900 household money holdings sourced.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: months of government revenue held as treasury cash
rows.note: No cross-country 1900 treasury balances sourced.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: share of non-education revenue funding civil administration
rows.note: The rest is military, pensions, interest and public works, which the sim funds through its own channels.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: daily route capacity as a share of the smaller market's covered value added per day
rows.note: Until bilateral 1900 trade (RICardo, Federico-Tena) is sourced.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: kilograms of fibre per kilogram of cloth
rows.note: Spinning and weaving waste of about 13%.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: kilograms of wheat per kilogram of flour
rows.note: 4 2/3 bushels (280 lb) of wheat per 196-lb barrel of flour; milling rule of thumb.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: garment price relative to its cloth content
rows.note: No 1900 garment price series sourced.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: capitalist households as a share of the US population
rows.note: The 1900 census has no capitalist class.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: jobs in one building level of the 1900 definitions
rows.note: Finer levels than the M11 definitions (25,000 jobs) so small territories can be calibrated.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: share of the food and apparel budget above the subsistence and basic tiers spent in the comfort tier
rows.note: Split between the comfort and luxury tiers.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: months of a laborer's wage per soldier's equipment
rows.note: A service rifle cost about a month's pay.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: annual equipment upkeep as a share of its price
rows.note: Provisional.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: days of soldier pay per recruitment
rows.note: Provisional signing cost.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: largest share of a territory's workforce of a profession employed at the 1900 start
rows.note: Where the food and apparel budget needs more workers than the authored occupation mix provides, technique is raised instead (owners keep the extra value added); leaves room for the employment refresh.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: woollen cloth priced with the cotton print cloth markup over its fibre
rows.note: No 1900 woollen cloth price series sourced; the sim's textiles are a cotton-wool composite.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: storage per warehouse level and good, kilograms
rows.note: One million bushels of wheat (60 lb), the order of a large 1900 terminal grain elevator; not sourced.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: market storage in days of its largest good's daily output
rows.note: Room for five days of unsold output before overflow.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: fish price relative to the cattle price per kilogram
rows.note: No 1900 fish price series sourced.

rows.subject: coefficient
rows.measure: freight per 1,000 km as a share of a good's base price
rows.note: The M11 rule, kept: near ocean rates and far below 1900 rail rates; to be sourced by mode in P8.

rows.measure: comfort-tier food budget share: processed food
rows.note: Provisional split by value.
